answer: Cap rewards per similarity cluster, not per identity: group answers, bids, and reviews by near-duplicate content and timing, then pay the cluster once and split it among its members. A sybil farm in one harbor can launch a thousand clones tending the same orchard, but they share one pot, so each extra copy dilutes its own return. Distinct work forms its own kernel and earns separately, making duplication self-defeating while real diversity pays.
